hero.title: The realm remembers.
hero.description: Enter a dark fantasy action RPG where dangerous magic, uneasy alliances and your choices shape the journey.
hero.intro: You survived what should have killed you. Beneath an old house, a mysterious Doll offers a way forward. Beyond its walls, villages cling to faith, a kingdom holds its breath, and something waits in the dark.

regions.name: The awakening
regions.description: A cage beneath an old house. A voice with answers of her own. Follow the Doll’s guidance into a village gathering, where even your first response can leave a lasting impression.

regions.name: Thornhallow
regions.description: A hidden community led by the Veyne sisters. Earn their trust, meet their withdrawn father and follow a family’s story from the quiet village to the heart of the Kingdom.

regions.name: Cairnhold
regions.description: Above the crowded streets, wealth and influence gather around the Crown. Below, ordinary people live with taxes, curfews and harsh justice—and the Thieves keep a society of their own.

regions.name: The Cult’s domain
regions.description: Ritual and sacrifice bind the Cult’s followers together. Seek answers among them, then face the ordeal waiting inside the Sixfold Crucible.

regions.name: Beyond the familiar
regions.description: The road reaches beyond the Kingdom: to the Templars of Iron Vow Hold, the Witch territories and the Plague Doctors who dwell there. Every place has its own loyalties.

characters.name: The Cursed Doll
characters.intro: A small companion with unsettling answers. She offers guidance, training and a way to travel—but trust is yours to give.
characters.detail: The Hidden Village’s ancestors created the Doll as a vessel for Dark magic. She gained a will of her own and now draws others toward bloodshed and ritual. The seal and the Doll are one and the same.

characters.name: Father Corven
characters.intro: A priest who found renewed faith in a mysterious power. His conviction reaches far beyond the church doors.
characters.detail: The Doll guided Corven to a Relief and the village. He believed sacrifice fed his god and brought salvation. Seeking the Demon Father, he summoned the Nun instead. What he believes and what he has helped cause are very different things.

characters.name: Elder Garran Veyne
characters.intro: A teacher of Holy magic who has sworn off casting. Reaching him means understanding the grief behind his retreat.
characters.detail: Garran accidentally harmed his wife with magic, and she died. He withdrew, leaving his daughters to lead the village. He can guide your own use of Holy magic, though he no longer casts it himself.

characters.name: Lucan Veyne
characters.intro: A master of Blood magic and protector of the King and Queen. His pursuit of power began with a wish to do good.
characters.detail: Garran’s son and the Veyne sisters’ brother, Lucan can become an ally against the Demon Father. If you march with the Cult, he stands as the Kingdom’s final defender. His Blood shield carries him and the royal couple to safety when the Kingdom falls.

characters.name: The Veyne daughters
characters.intro: Tressa and Nerys lead Thornhallow. Get to know each sister: their trust and their support must be earned individually.
characters.detail: They are Garran’s daughters and Lucan’s sisters. After their mother’s death and their father’s withdrawal, they took responsibility for the village. Earning one sister’s support does not automatically earn the other’s.

characters.name: The Nun
characters.intro: A supernatural presence whose appearances lead you deeper into the mystery surrounding the village.
characters.detail: Corven’s summoning brought the Nun into the story. The attic and Crucible encounters take you through memories; her later sacrifice at the End Church brings forth the Demon Father.

characters.name: Pell
characters.intro: At the Opera Hall, your past adventures become performances—and the audience has opinions.
characters.detail: Behind the Changelings lies the Opera Hall, where Pell stages stories from quests you have completed. Return to see familiar events in a different light.

schools.description: Heal wounds, strengthen your defenses and hold enemies in place. Protect yourself—or support the people fighting beside you.
Turn your own health into power. Drain your enemies, move faster, summon a demon or protect yourself with a Blood Barrier.
Disappear, terrify your enemies and control the battlefield. Each cast brings you closer to lasting corruption.

faq.a: A dark fantasy action RPG about exploration, physical combat, powerful magic and personal choices. Travel through troubled communities, build relationships and decide where you stand.
Eclipsed Realms is in development. Release timing, supported platforms and where to buy the game have not been announced.
The campaign supports up to four players, with up to two local players on each machine. Join over a local network or with a direct address.

faq.q: Do we have to make the same choices?
faq.a: No. Your answers, relationships and personal consequences belong to your character. The host’s choices determine what physically happens in the shared world.

faq.q: Are Holy and Blood magic good and evil?
faq.a: A school of magic does not decide your morality. Holy magic can cause harm, and Blood magic can protect. Your actions tell your story.

faq.q: Will the guide spoil the story?
faq.a: The main site introduces the world without revealing its endings. Quest details, character secrets and ending explanations stay behind an optional spoiler switch on World & story.

faq.q: Where should I start with the guide?
faq.a: Begin with How to play for combat, magic and exploration essentials. Use the Player guide when you want details on a particular spell, weapon, ability or game system.

faq.q: Do I need to enter training to unlock fast travel?
faq.a: No. Discover a Doll travel destination during your journey to make it available. The station at the old house opens after its attic story encounter.

decisions.title: The hanging
decisions.setup: Two villagers are about to be hanged. Do you speak against the execution or support it?
decisions.consequence: Both villagers die. The game remembers whether you opposed or encouraged their deaths.
decisions.after: Nella’s later request about a runaway is a separate choice; it does not add another moral vote.

decisions.title: The courier
decisions.setup: Cultists have captured a courier. You can try to save him or encourage his captors.
decisions.consequence: The courier dies in either case. Your attempt to help still counts as a Good answer.
decisions.after: The captors and factions react to the answer you gave.

decisions.title: The village gate
decisions.setup: A wounded deserter asks for shelter. His pursuers demand that the village hand him over.
decisions.consequence: Protecting Iven gives him sanctuary. Surrendering him sends him away with Rusk in exchange for payment.
decisions.after: The daughters react when you return to the gate.

decisions.title: The royal hearing
decisions.setup: Evidence suggests Mara was coerced. The King asks for your judgment.
decisions.consequence: Defending Mara leads to house confinement and an investigation, not a pardon. Supporting the sentence condemns her and sends the evidence for destruction.
decisions.after: The Queen responds to what happened at the hearing.

decisions.title: The ritual
decisions.setup: Rusk is taking a captive’s breath into a vessel. You can break the connection or help him finish.
decisions.consequence: Breaking the connection lets Tamsin escape. Helping Rusk completes the draw; Tamsin goes still.
decisions.after: You can return to see what remains after the ritual.

quests.title: The Courier in the Ring
quests.description: Cultists near Vesper Hollow are holding a captured Kingdom courier. He will not live through the night, whatever I do. What I do decides what I am to both sides.

quests.title: A Candle for the Chosen
quests.description: The church in Vesper Hollow is preparing a Candle, a rite that spends a willing young woman's life for a season of hope. Ysolde wants hands. What I do with the girl and with the Hollow Lantern decides what the church becomes.

quests.title: The Names on the Rope
quests.description: Start Village is hanging two of its own, Mara and Oren Venn, for sheltering a woman who fled the church. They will die whatever I do. I must say, plainly, whether I stand against the hanging or cheer it, and the village will remember which.

quests.title: What the Road Offers
quests.description: A man in a grey hood is sharing bread at the roadside. He is not offering it for free.

quests.title: A Price for Silence
quests.description: A Cult envoy has found the Hidden Village, and I led him to its door. He offers a bargain, and every answer costs someone.

quests.title: Papers and Names
quests.description: At the gate of Cairnhold a captain wants a refugee handed over on suspicion of Cult ties.

quests.title: The Armory Keys
quests.description: Someone in the Lower City watch is selling the armory keys. The man who knows is afraid to say it twice.

quests.title: Bread and Torches
quests.description: The Lower City riots over bread while the Queen's writ waits to reach the palace.

quests.title: The Door We Keep
quests.description: Decide whether a wounded Cult deserter is sheltered or handed to his pursuers.

quests.title: The Gate, Afterward
quests.description: Return to the daughters after the sanctuary dispute.

quests.title: The King's Justice
quests.description: Examine the evidence against Mara before the King passes judgment.

quests.title: The Cost of a Witness
quests.description: Speak to Queen Sicilian after the hearing.

quests.title: The Ritual
quests.description: Confront a ritual that feeds a living captive’s breath into a vessel.

quests.title: What the Vessel Kept
quests.description: Return to the ritual court.

quests.title: A Child in the Woods
quests.description: A boy is crying alone in the forest. He says he is lost.

quests.title: A Seat at Their Table
quests.description: The boy's sister welcomed us inside. She says their mother is upstairs.

quests.title: Behind the House
quests.description: The household's welcome was a trap. Beyond the house stands an Opera House, but a Wendigo blocks the way between the buildings.

quests.title: What Faith Cannot Teach
quests.description: The Priest spoke of an old man in Thornhallow who knows another form of Holy invocation. I should ask whether he will teach me.

quests.title: The Old Man's Trial
quests.description: The Old Man asked me to hunt one moose, one goat, one cow or bull, one bear, and one deer, collect their skulls, then return to him.

quests.title: A Place Still Kept
quests.description: The Old Man's daughters asked me to speak with their brother in Cairnhold. They want him to come home. I promised to ask and bring back his answer.

quests.title: The Doors We Closed
quests.description: The village is empty. A record inside one of the surviving homes may explain what happened.

quests.title: Those the Earth Refused
quests.description: The gravekeeper has buried people whose families refused to identify them publicly.

quests.title: The Unspoken Confession
quests.description: The parish register records disappearances without explaining where the people went.

quests.title: Shelter at a Price
quests.description: Lenna's family traded possessions and labor for shelter.

quests.title: The Mercy of the Knife
quests.description: Some people remember Doctor Malven as the only person who helped them.

quests.title: The Oath That Outlived Death
quests.description: The Templars once pledged to protect the living.

quests.title: The Faith We Keep
quests.description: Caldra has helped vulnerable residents without waiting for official approval.

quests.title: Honor Among the Forgotten
quests.description: Rook has a record of confiscated property and inflated collections.

quests.title: Left Behind
quests.description: Dain left a warning inside the dungeon passage.

quests.title: Beneath Their Feet
quests.description: A sewer receipt lists supplies taken from Lower City households.

quests.title: Bread for Tomorrow
quests.description: Marta's household was charged repeatedly against the same collection order.

quests.title: When the Bells Ring
quests.description: The invasion has reached the city. The people I met are caught in the evacuation.

quests.title: The Royal Seal
quests.description: The supplementary collection carries Vael's mark but exceeds the lawful order.

quests.title: What the Dead Remember
quests.description: Speak to the Doll.

quests.title: The First Death
quests.description: Speak to the Doll near the attic.

quests.title: A Village at Prayer
quests.description: Pass through the tavern.

quests.title: Worthy of the Offering
quests.description: I accepted the Priest's challenge to survive the six-demon ordeal and prove myself through it.

quests.title: An End to the Offering
quests.description: I told the Priest I would end the Arena's six-demon ordeal. I intend to stop what waits there, not celebrate it.

quests.title: Six Graves Open
quests.description: A woman kneels in the center of the Arena.

quests.title: When the Seal Weeps
quests.description: With the sixth demon's death, the sealed door of the Church of the Last Vigil no longer holds. My attention was drawn back to the ossuary beneath the old house. Something there remains unfinished.

quests.title: The Crown Must Fall
quests.description: Witness the summoning.

quests.title: No More Offerings
quests.description: Defeat the Demon Father.

entries.title: Damage and armor
entries.summary: Attack Rating strengthens your hits; Armor reduces the damage you take.
body: Attack damage increases with Attack Rating, then is reduced by the target’s Armor and the material you hit. Armor is a reduction in proportion to the hit: 100 Armor halves this part of the damage calculation, while 200 Armor reduces it to one third.
Critical hits, attacks from behind, weapon bonuses, protection effects and armor-family benefits can change the final result. Bleeds and other ongoing effects may follow their own rules.
Physical and Magic are different damage types. Holy, Blood and Dark are magic schools. A strike with a held Relief board deals physical damage.

entries.title: Critical hits
entries.summary: Stealth Rating improves your chance to land a critical hit.
body: The basic critical chance rises from 5% at Stealth Rating 0 to 32.5% at 100. Stealth perks can add further chances when you attack an unaware enemy.
Weapon-technique criticals deal 1.5 times normal damage before dagger bonuses. One wielded base dagger raises that multiplier to 1.65; two raise it to 1.80.

entries.title: Choose your armor
entries.summary: Armor families offer different protection and healing benefits.
body: Knight and Templar pieces reduce bow damage. Thief and Guard pieces reduce one-handed, unarmed and held-Relief melee damage. Caster armor reduces magic damage. Tattered and Villager clothing improve healing received from magic and food.

Each matching piece adds 3 percentage points to its family benefit. Five pieces give 15%; mixed sets contribute only their matching pieces. These benefits are separate from the Armor number on your equipment.
A wielded shield also reduces two-handed weapon damage by 7%. Druid armor has no additional family protection or healing bonus.

entries.title: Blocking
entries.summary: Face the attack and guard to reduce its damage.
body: An ordinary block protects a 90-degree cone in front of you. Attacks from the side or rear receive no guard bonus.
Your guard adds Armor for the blocked hit. Shields give the strongest bonus at +300. Swords, axes and daggers give +150; a torch gives +15; bows, unarmed guards and Relief boards give +10.
When you wield two weapons, only the stronger guard bonus applies. Watch your Stamina: a block you cannot afford breaks your guard.

entries.title: Shield parries
entries.summary: Raise your shield in time with an attacker’s glow to turn defense into an opening.
body: A shield-block press opens a half-second parry window. For a melee parry, time that press to the attacker’s visible glow. Successful parries prevent the hit and stagger the attacker, but still spend the normal blocked-hit Stamina cost.
You can also parry ordinary arrows. This prevents their damage without staggering the archer or building Balance.
Magic, weapon techniques and physical Ultimates cannot be parried. Weapon techniques and physical Ultimates can still be blocked.

entries.title: Guard break
entries.summary: Running out of Stamina leaves your guard open.
body: If a blocked hit costs more Stamina than you have left, that attack lands without the guard Armor bonus. Your remaining Stamina falls to zero and your block and parry window end.
A guard break also staggers you for one second unless you have protection against that stagger. This is separate from the Balance break caused by repeated parries.

entries.title: Balance and disarming
entries.summary: Repeated melee parries can break an attacker’s posture and knock away a weapon.
body: Each successful melee parry adds 40 Balance to the attacker. At 100, their posture breaks: three parries can do it if they have not recovered enough between them. Ordinary hits do not add Balance.
Balance begins recovering after five seconds without further Balance damage, then falls by three points per second. A break staggers for 1.5 seconds and can drop a weapon.
Players and bosses can be disarmed this way. Ordinary elite enemies are protected from Balance disarming, and a target already disarmed will not drop another weapon through this effect.

entries.title: Counter after a parry
entries.summary: Follow a successful parry with a lunge or heavy counterattack.
body: After parrying a melee attack, press attack to counter toward the enemy you parried.

A heavy counter that lands within the opening can knock that attacker down. The opening lasts at least 1.8 seconds, or longer when the parry stagger lasts longer. A knocked-down enemy remains on the ground for 1.6 seconds before getting up.

entries.title: Weapon bonuses
entries.summary: The weapons you wield bring bonuses beyond their active attacks.
body: Only weapons you are wielding contribute their bonuses. Main-hand and offhand contributions add together, while two-handed swords and axes contribute twice their family’s normal amount.

Swords pierce armor, axes improve bleeding, daggers strengthen technique criticals, shields resist bleed and bows choose a bonus on each ordinary arrow hit. Enemies can benefit from their wielded weapons too.
Weapon mastery improves these passive bonuses. Mastering a technique does not automatically grant passive weapon mastery.

entries.title: Sword: pierce armor
entries.summary: Swords help ordinary weapon hits get through an enemy’s Armor.
body: One sword ignores 15% of the target’s Armor, rising to 20% with weapon mastery. A greatsword contributes twice as much: 30%, or 40% when mastered.
Bonuses from wielded weapons add together, up to 100%. This reduces the Armor value used against the hit; it does not remove the target’s separate armor-family protection.

entries.title: Axes and blunt weapons: bleed
entries.summary: Axe-family hits leave a bleed, and wielded axes strengthen bleeding damage.
body: An ordinary axe-family hit bleeds for 5% of the health damage it caused over four seconds. Wielding an axe adds 15% to your bleed damage, or 20% with weapon mastery. Two-handed axes contribute 30%, or 40% mastered. Blunt weapons share this family bonus.
Each application lasts independently. A 100-damage hit with a base one-handed axe produces 5.75 bleed damage before the target’s further reductions.
A shield can reduce bleeding while it is wielded. Equipping or dropping it changes subsequent bleed damage. Armor is not applied a second time to this passive bleed.

entries.title: Dagger: stronger technique criticals
entries.summary: Wielded daggers increase the damage of critical weapon techniques.
body: Each dagger adds 0.15 to the critical multiplier, or 0.20 with weapon mastery. A normal 1.50-times technique critical becomes 1.65 with one base dagger or 1.80 with two.

entries.title: Shield: resist bleeding
entries.summary: A wielded shield reduces bleed damage and helps against two-handed attacks.
body: Shields reduce incoming weapon bleed by 20%, or 30% with weapon mastery. This applies to ordinary weapon bleeds and technique bleeds.
A shield also reduces two-handed damage by 7%. When you actively block a frontal hit, it adds +300 Armor. These are three separate benefits.

entries.title: Bow: pierce or bleed
entries.summary: Each ordinary arrow has an equal chance to pierce armor or leave a bleed.
body: An arrow either ignores 7.5% of the target’s Armor or bleeds for 7.5% of the health damage it caused over five seconds. Weapon mastery raises the chosen effect to 10%.
Axe bonuses do not increase bow bleeding, but a wielded shield still reduces it.

entries.title: Torch: burning hits
entries.summary: A wielded torch adds burning damage to ordinary weapon hits.
body: The base burn deals 20% of the torch’s Attack Power over five seconds; an upgraded torch burn deals 40%. Each torch in your hands adds its own burn.
Blocked hits, techniques and ongoing burn or bleed damage do not trigger this ordinary-hit bonus. Torch Sweep and torch Ultimates have their own fire effects.

entries.title: Attack from the shadows
entries.summary: Blindside rewards direct hits from behind; Shadow Step can make the opening stronger.
body: Blindside adds 7.5%, 15% or 25% damage at its three ranks when a direct hit lands inside the 70-degree rear arc. Ongoing bleeds do not receive this bonus, and a blocking enemy does not grant it.

At rank 2, Shadow Step adds 50 percentage points to your next qualifying rear hit against the enemy you stepped behind. Land it within five seconds. Combined with Blindside rank 3, that strike gains 75% rear damage.

entries.title: Unseen Edge and Silent Opening
entries.summary: Crouch and catch an unaware enemy for a stronger chance to strike critically.
body: Unseen Edge adds 50 percentage points to critical chance while you crouch against an enemy that is not alert to you. A 10% chance becomes 60%.
Silent Opening adds 100 percentage points on the first qualifying attack against that enemy, guaranteeing a critical. After it becomes aware of you, a later unaware encounter can offer a new opening.
An attack that already scores a critical does not receive a second critical multiplier.

entries.title: Effects that change damage
entries.summary: Mastered spells and combat abilities can change how much damage you deal or receive.
body: Mastered Fear makes its target take 20% more damage. Mastered Binding Light makes its rooted target deal 20% less damage.
Mastered Dark Ascension increases your Dark damage by 35% and reduces incoming damage by 25%. Pet Mastery increases pet damage by 50%, while Reaver’s Fury increases physical damage by 30%.
Applicable damage bonuses and reductions multiply together. Damage immunity prevents damage altogether.

entries.title: Make healing go further
entries.summary: Your clothing and Karma can improve the healing you receive.
body: Each Tattered or Villager piece increases healing from magic and food by 3%. Five matching pieces give 15%. This bonus does not apply to equipment regeneration or revival.

At Karma 25 or higher, Holy healing received increases by 25%; at Karma 50 or higher, it increases by 50%. This multiplies with the armor-family benefit. Food and regeneration do not receive the Karma bonus.
Pets can recover through Holy healing and regeneration, but not food, Blood healing or Dark healing. A dead pet needs revival.

entries.title: Fight beneath an eclipse
entries.summary: An eclipse strengthens magic and changes the cost of some spells.
body: At full eclipse, Holy, Blood and Dark Relief damage gain 15%. A solar eclipse increases Dark damage by 25% in total and strengthens Dark effects by a further 10%.
Full eclipse reduces Holy and Blood Stamina costs by 10%. A lunar eclipse also reduces Blood health sacrifices by 20%. Dark Stamina costs do not change.

Empowered creatures gain 15% damage under a full lunar eclipse or 25% under a full solar eclipse. These benefits grow with eclipse strength. A creature casting a school spell uses the larger applicable damage bonus rather than adding both together.

entries.title: Execution finishers
entries.summary: An execution can finish an eligible foe, but cannot bypass invulnerability.
body: When an execution reaches its finishing strike, it deals enough damage to kill an eligible target. Invulnerable enemies remain protected, and key final encounters cannot be skipped with an execution.

entries.title: Flurry
entries.summary: Four rapid strikes with a short forward burst.
body: Close the distance with a short lunge, then strike four times. Each strike contributes an equal share of the total damage.
The lunge reaches 1.7 metres, or 2.2 metres when enhanced.
Paired values show base strength → enhanced strength. Damage is a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

entries.title: Sundering Thrust
entries.summary: A lunging thrust that ignores part of the target’s armor.
body: Thrust forward at one enemy and ignore 35% of their Armor, rising to 50% when enhanced.
The lunge reaches 2.4 metres, or 2.6 metres when enhanced.
Paired values show base strength → enhanced strength. Damage is a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

entries.title: Rending Cleave
entries.summary: A frontal cleave that leaves a bleed.
body: Cleave through up to three enemies ahead of you. In addition to the initial hit, the wound bleeds for 40% of Attack Power over five seconds, rising to 70% when enhanced.
Paired values show base strength → enhanced strength. Damage is a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

entries.title: Executioner's Arc
entries.summary: A broad frontal sweep through nearby enemies.
body: Sweep a broad arc in front of you, hitting every enemy in reach. The strike covers the forward arc rather than a full circle.
Paired values show base strength → enhanced strength. Damage is a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

stats.label: Reach and targets
stats.value: 140° → 165° cone · 3.2 → 3.3 m · all targets in the area

entries.title: Falling Ruin
entries.summary: An overhead strike with a small impact area.
body: Bring the greataxe down in a small impact area ahead of you. Every enemy in the circle can be hit.
Paired values show base strength → enhanced strength. Damage is a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

entries.title: Arrowstorm
entries.summary: An aimed rain of arrows delivered in waves.
body: Aim a rain of arrows at an area. Five waves share the total damage, striking every enemy caught within the area.
Paired values show base strength → enhanced strength. Damage is a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

entries.title: Skullcrusher
entries.summary: A crushing overhead blow that staggers one foe.
body: Commit to an overhead blow against one enemy. The hit also staggers for 1.5 seconds before the target’s protections.
Paired values show base strength → enhanced strength. Damage is a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

stats.label: Reach and targets
stats.value: Impact 1.9 → 2 m ahead · radius 0.9 → 1 m · 1 target

entries.title: Torch Sweep
entries.summary: A wide torch swipe followed by a second burn application.
body: Sweep the torch through up to four enemies. The first burn deals 20% of Attack Power over five seconds, or 40% when enhanced.
Two seconds later, a second burn begins independently. It deals half the first burn’s damage at base strength, or the same damage when enhanced.
Paired values show base strength → enhanced strength. Damage is a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

entries.title: Savage Combination
entries.summary: Hook, cross, knee and a finishing kick.
body: Chain a hook, cross, knee and finishing kick. Their damage shares are 30%, 35%, 45% and 90% of unarmed Attack Power.
The final kick knocks ordinary targets back. Elite enemies are pushed less; bosses are not displaced. Savage Combination has one strength tier.
Damage is shown as a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

entries.title: King's Reprisal
entries.summary: A guarded stance that answers an incoming hit with a shield bash.
body: Use the offhand technique to raise a guarded stance for 1.5 seconds. An incoming strike triggers a counter bash. If nothing triggers it, the stance ends with a forward bash.
The bash staggers for half a second before protections. King’s Reprisal has one strength tier.
Damage is shown as a percentage of Attack Power before defenses.

stats.label: Damage
stats.value: 150% Attack Power bash · 250% Attack Power counter

stats.label: Reach and targets
stats.value: 1.5 s guard · 2.2 m bash · 3.5 m counter

entries.title: Final Whisper
entries.summary: A closing dash and lethal two-strike combination.
body: Dash forward into two strikes against one enemy. The first deals 35% of the total and the second deals 65%. Strike from directly behind for increased damage.
The lunge covers 2.2 metres and the attack reaches 2.6 metres.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Duelist's Verdict
entries.summary: Three measured strikes against the enemy ahead.
body: Lunge into three strikes: 135%, 135% and 180% of Attack Power. Each strike can hit one target.
The lunge covers 0.8 metres and the strikes reach 2.6 metres.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Reaver's Fury
entries.summary: A short weapon-damage, movement and heavy-cleave buff.
body: For eight seconds, gain 30% physical damage, 20% movement speed and resistance to minor interruptions.
Heavy attacks cleave a 150-degree arc out to three metres, using your wielded weapon’s heavy-attack damage.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Bonebreaker
entries.summary: A committed armor-piercing overhead blow.
body: Bring your greataxe down on one foe with 25 additional percentage points of armor penetration. The attack reaches 1.9 metres.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Grave Procession
entries.summary: Two broad sweeps and a final downward cleave.
body: Lunge forward 1.2 metres, then cut through a 140-degree arc with two sweeps and a final cleave. Each enemy in the 3.2-metre reach can take all three strikes: 150%, 150% and 225% of Attack Power.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Earthshatter
entries.summary: A ground slam that damages and staggers enemies around you.
body: Slam the ground in a full circle with a 4.5-metre radius, centered slightly ahead of you. Every enemy caught in it takes damage and a two-second stagger before protections.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: The Last Arrow
entries.summary: A precise shot that pierces several enemies.
body: Fire a precise shot up to 40 metres through as many as four enemies. Each enemy after the first takes 70% of the previous enemy’s damage.
The shot gains 25 additional percentage points of armor penetration. Walls and terrain stop it.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Funeral Pyre
entries.summary: A burning sweep followed by a short ground fire.
body: Sweep a 150-degree arc out to three metres, burning every enemy in reach. The special burn is twice the ordinary torch burn.
Leave a 2.6-metre circle of ground fire ahead of you. It deals four bursts of 25% Attack Power over two seconds.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Shove
entries.summary: Throw one enemy back and keep it down briefly.
body: Shove one enemy up to 3.5 metres away. It stays down for two seconds before beginning to rise. Elite enemies stagger instead.
The shove reaches 2.2 metres and deals no direct damage.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Gutter Cut
entries.summary: A finishing stab followed by a deep bleed.
body: Learn this alternate dagger Ultimate from Mardo the Knife. Lunge 1.2 metres into a finishing stab against one enemy.
The wound then bleeds for 250% of Attack Power over ten seconds.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Repelling Blow
entries.summary: A wide sweep that hurls enemies backward.
body: Learn this alternate greataxe Ultimate from the Templar teacher. Sweep a 140-degree arc out to six metres, hurling enemies back and staggering them for 0.6 seconds before protections.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Viper's Volley
entries.summary: Three poisoned arrows fired in a narrow fan.
body: Learn this alternate bow Ultimate from Vessa Thornquill. Fire three arrows in a narrow fan, with six degrees between them.

Each arrow can pierce up to four enemies over a 40-metre range. Damage falls to 70% at each subsequent target. Poison lasts six seconds; a new application refreshes it instead of stacking. Bleed bonuses do not strengthen this poison.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

stats.label: Damage
stats.value: 120% Attack Power per arrow + 180% Attack Power poison

entries.title: Gatebreaker
entries.summary: A lunging line attack that breaks guards and knocks down enemies.
body: Learn this alternate greatsword Ultimate from Sergeant Holt Varrow. Lunge 2.5 metres and thrust through a five-metre line, hitting every enemy caught in its width.
The attack breaks guards and knocks enemies back 2.5 metres while knocking them down.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Hewer's Tithe
entries.summary: Two chops followed by a wide bleeding cleave.
body: Learn this alternate axe Ultimate from Maren Ashgrove. Strike twice for 120% Attack Power, then finish with a 200% cleave.
The final strike widens to a 140-degree arc, reaches 2.6 metres and applies an eight-second bleed worth 150% of Attack Power.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Plague Censer
entries.summary: A crushing blow that leaves a poisoning cloud.
body: Learn this alternate blunt-weapon Ultimate from Doctor Ilsabet Mourne. A crushing strike leaves a poison cloud four metres across its radius for six seconds.
Poison lasts six seconds and refreshes while enemies remain in the cloud.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

stats.label: Damage
stats.value: 250% Attack Power direct · 160% Attack Power poison

entries.title: Valiant Charge
entries.summary: An invulnerable dash that slashes enemies along its path.
body: Learn this alternate sword Ultimate from Ser Alaric Dunmere. Dash six metres, slashing every enemy along the path.
You are invulnerable during the 0.6-second dash.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Cinder Spiral
entries.summary: A full spin followed by a ring of ground fire.
body: Learn this alternate torch Ultimate from Initiate Sorrel. Spin through enemies within three metres, then leave a four-metre ring of fire for two seconds.
The direct spin adds no separate special burn; the ground fire delivers four bursts of 25% Attack Power.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

stats.label: Damage
stats.value: 180% Attack Power direct + 4 × 25% Attack Power ground ticks

entries.title: Disarm
entries.summary: Wrench away a wielded weapon and drop it into the world.
body: Learn this alternate unarmed Ultimate from Old Brannoc. Reach 2.2 metres to wrench away an enemy’s wielded weapon and drop it on the ground.
The move applies an eight-second disarm and a 0.8-second stagger. It can affect players, ordinary enemies, elites and bosses, but blocking or protection from knockback can prevent the weapon drop.
Damage percentages use Attack Power before defenses. Physical Ultimates have a single strength tier.

entries.title: Lesser Heal
entries.summary: A quick self-heal, shared with nearby allies when mastered.
body: Heal yourself when the flare arrives: 20% of maximum Health, or 35% when enhanced. You normally need to be injured to cast.
Mastery also heals eligible allies in the Relief’s aura for 35% of their own maximum Health. You can cast at full Health if an ally in the aura is hurt.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Greater Heal
entries.summary: A stronger self-heal carried by a flare.
body: A stronger healing flare restores 45% of your maximum Health, or 80% when enhanced.
Mastery also heals eligible allies in the Relief’s aura for 80% of their own maximum Health. You can cast at full Health if an ally in the aura is hurt.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Holy Armor
entries.summary: Surround yourself with an Armor blessing.
body: Gain +300 Armor for 20 seconds, rising to +500 when enhanced. Holy Armor reduces damage through Armor; it does not make you invulnerable.
Mastery shares +500 Armor with eligible allies inside the Relief’s aura when the spell releases.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Binding Light
entries.summary: A forward wedge that roots enemies.
body: Send light through a wedge ten metres long and five metres wide at its far edge. It roots enemies for five seconds, or eight seconds when enhanced. Rooted enemies can still turn and act.
Mastery also reduces the rooted enemies’ damage dealt by 20%.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Divine Renewal
entries.summary: A sustained heal over time.
body: Restore 8% of your maximum Health each second for eight seconds, rising to 15% when enhanced.
Mastery also heals eligible allies inside the Relief’s aura for 15% of their own maximum Health per second. Leaving the aura pauses their healing; returning resumes it.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Old Man's Blessing
entries.summary: Immediate healing, regeneration and armor in one blessing.
body: Restore 45% of maximum Health immediately, then 6% per second for eight seconds. Enhanced, this becomes 80% immediately and 11.25% per second. Gain +300 Armor, or +500 enhanced, for 20 seconds. This Armor stacks with Holy Armor.
Mastery shares the complete blessing with eligible allies in the Relief’s aura, using each recipient’s maximum Health. Repeated blessings do not double an existing regeneration or Armor benefit.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Blood Offering
entries.summary: Sacrifice Health for regeneration, Attack Power and Armor.
body: Sacrifice Health for a 30-second blessing. It restores 25% of maximum Health over that time and grants +100 Attack Power and +200 Armor. Enhanced, these become 45% healing, +175 Attack Power and +350 Armor.
Mastery also heals you for 50% of the damage you actually deal while Offering lasts, including weapons, spells and damage over time.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Blood Siphon
entries.summary: Drain tethered enemies around the Relief and restore your Health.
body: Tether enemies within 50 metres of the Relief when the spell releases. For five seconds, drain 2% of each living target’s maximum Health every half-second, rising to 3.5% when enhanced. You recover the Health actually drained after defenses.
Mastery slows tethered enemies by 50%. With Blood Offering active, the combined healing return becomes 150% of the drained Health.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Blood Rush
entries.summary: Move faster and reposition through danger.
body: Move 25% faster for 15 seconds, or 45% faster when enhanced.
Mastery also increases Stamina regeneration by 50% while the rush lasts.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Blood Rupture
entries.summary: Strike a long lane extending from the Relief toward your aim.
body: Strike a lane 25 metres long and three metres wide from the Relief toward your aim. Deal 150% of Attack Power to enemies in the lane, rising to 275% when enhanced.
Mastery leaves surviving targets bleeding for half the damage they actually took, spread over five seconds.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Summon Demon
entries.summary: A demon emerges from the deployed Relief and follows its summoner.
body: Call one demon from your deployed Relief. It follows you for 45 seconds or until killed. Enhancement gives it 75% more Health and damage.

Mastery lets the demon remain until killed, doubles its base maximum Health and keeps the enhanced damage bonus. It takes 20% of damage that would hit you and dies if you die. You cannot summon a second demon while it is alive.
Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Blood Barrier
entries.summary: A Health sacrifice buys a period of true invulnerability.
body: Sacrifice half your maximum Health for 30 seconds of invulnerability, or 40 seconds when enhanced. Harmful effects are blocked, but your own Relief casting costs still apply.
Mastery reduces the sacrifice to 35% of maximum Health. It also slows enemies within 35 metres at release by 35% for the barrier’s duration.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Invisibility
entries.summary: Conceal yourself and regenerate Health.
body: Conceal yourself for ten seconds and restore 20% of maximum Health over that time. Enhancement increases this to 15 seconds and 30% healing.
Mastery gives one second of full damage immunity as invisibility begins.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Void Pulse
entries.summary: Push away enemies around the Relief and knock them down.
body: Knock down enemies within 25 metres of the Relief and push them away. The push reaches ten metres, or 16 metres when enhanced, before further bonuses. Terrain can stop it early.
Mastery prevents a pushed target from moving for five seconds after it finishes getting up. It can still act during this movement slow.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Fear
entries.summary: Send nearby enemies fleeing.
body: Send enemies within 15 metres of the Relief fleeing for five seconds, or nine seconds when enhanced.
Mastery extends the fear to 13.5 seconds and makes affected enemies take 20% more damage.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Curse
entries.summary: A single-target curse selected from enemies visible to the Relief.
body: Curse one enemy within 25 metres and visible to the Relief. Over ten seconds it deals 20% of the target’s maximum Health, or 35% when enhanced, before defenses and boss adjustments.

Mastery moves some damage from the early pulses into a stronger final pulse without changing the total. When the curse ends, or the target dies early, it can transfer once to another enemy within five metres for a full new duration.
Paired values show base → enhanced strength. Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Void Stasis
entries.summary: Freeze the battlefield around your Relief.
body: A falling void orb freezes other combat characters within 50 metres of the Relief for five seconds. The caster is excluded. Your cost and cooldown begin when you release the spell, before the orb lands.
Mastery extends the freeze to 7.5 seconds and reduces the base cooldown to 35 seconds.
Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Dark Ascension
entries.summary: Rise above the fight and unleash heavy Dark projectiles.
body: Rise into a hovering form for 20 seconds. Attack releases a heavy Dark projectile: 125% Attack Power on the direct target, with half that damage splashing within 1.5 metres. Shots release every three seconds after a one-second windup.

Begin on firm ground. The hover stays about two metres high within an eight-metre horizontal leash. You must remain in Dark Relief influence to fire; leaving it gives you two seconds to return before the form ends.
Mastery extends the form to 40 seconds, raises Dark damage by 35%, reduces incoming damage by 25% and halves the cooldowns of other Dark spells released while transformed.
Eclipse effects and your character’s bonuses can alter the final result.

entries.title: Techniques and Ultimates
entries.summary: Build a fighting style around weapon techniques and powerful finishing abilities.
body: Each weapon family offers a technique. Physical Ultimates follow your main-hand weapon family; shields have a technique but no physical Ultimate.

All physical techniques share one cooldown. All physical Ultimates share a separate cooldown, so using a technique does not lock out your Ultimate. Switching weapons or respawning does not reset these cooldowns.
Unlock a family’s default Ultimate through its perk, or learn an alternate and select it for that family. Technique mastery improves techniques; physical Ultimates have one strength tier.
Techniques cost 50 Stamina and physical Ultimates cost 100. Both can be blocked, but cannot be parried.

entries.title: The cost of magic
entries.summary: Holy spends Stamina. Blood sacrifices Health. Dark power leaves a lasting mark.
body: Holy spells use Stamina. Most Blood spells use Stamina and a percentage of maximum Health. You must have more Health than the sacrifice, so casting costs cannot kill you.
Dark spells add Dark Points instead of spending a mana pool. Reaching 100 permanently corrupts your character.
Each school has four regular spells and an Ultimate slot with two choices. A school’s Ultimates share a cooldown, so swapping them does not bypass it. Each school keeps its own Ultimate cooldown.
Unlock spells by rank, enhance them, then master them. Costs and cooldowns begin when the spell visibly releases. Eclipses, corruption and other bonuses can modify those costs and cooldowns.

stats.label: Each school
stats.value: 4 regular spells + a choice of 2 Ultimates

entries.title: Know your status effects
entries.summary: Root, freeze, fear and stagger create different openings.
body: Root stops movement but leaves attacks and turning available. Freeze stops both movement and actions. Slow reduces movement speed without freezing you.
Fear sends enemies fleeing and prevents their attacks until it ends. Knockdown includes the push, time on the ground and getting up. Stagger interrupts and prevents attacks during the recoil.
Fear from another allied player adds its duration to an existing Fear. Other overlapping Fear casts keep the longest remaining effect.

entries.title: Control and resistance
entries.summary: An enemy’s rank alone does not tell you which control effects will work.
body: Boss or Elite rank does not automatically grant immunity to every control effect. Individual attacks and protections can still shorten or prevent a particular effect.
Check each ability’s limits: heavy attacks, shoves and disarms can affect ordinary enemies, elites and bosses differently.

entries.title: Ongoing damage and drains
entries.summary: Curses, bleeds and tethers keep pressure on enemies after the first cast.
body: Curse damages its target over time. Blood Siphon drains enemies linked to the Relief. Mastered Blood Rupture leaves survivors bleeding.
Mastered Fear increases damage taken by 20%, while mastered Binding Light reduces the rooted target’s damage by 20%. Mastered Blood Offering turns damage you deal into healing.

entries.title: Protection and blessings
entries.summary: Magic can protect, restore and empower you as well as harm enemies.
body: Holy Armor strengthens your defense. Divine Renewal restores Health over time. Blood Offering combines healing, Attack Power and Armor, while Blood Rush increases movement speed.

Dark Invisibility conceals you and restores Health. Blood Barrier grants invulnerability while still charging your own spell costs. Mastered Dark Ascension increases Dark damage by 35% and reduces incoming damage by 25%.
Old Man’s Blessing provides its own Armor benefit, which can stack with Holy Armor.

entries.title: Tame a companion
entries.summary: Earn an animal’s trust and bring one pet on your journey.
body: Animal Taming rank 1 allows goats, deer, moose and cows. Rank 2 adds bears and mutant bears. Demon Goats and Minotaurs require rank 4 and a corrupted character.
Hold the taming interaction for two seconds, then remain through the three-second taming period within 4.5 metres. Your old pet is released only when the new bond succeeds.
You can have one pet. It follows your level and does not earn its own experience, Karma or criminal record.

entries.title: Strengthen your pet
entries.summary: Taming Mastery improves your pet’s health, recovery and damage.
body: Rank 1 gives 20% more maximum Health. Rank 2 raises regeneration from 5% to 10% of maximum Health per second. Rank 3 increases damage by 50%.
Holy healing and regeneration can heal pets. Food, Blood healing and Dark healing cannot. A dead pet needs revival.
Pets normally choose threats, but favor your target when either you or the pet falls below 35% Health. A pet left far behind can catch up beside you.

entries.title: Revive or dismiss a pet
entries.summary: Reach a fallen pet within five minutes to restore the bond.
body: Hold the revive interaction for five seconds at your pet’s revival site. It returns with 15% Health and takes three seconds to get up. The revival window can remain after the body disappears; after five minutes, the pet is lost.
Your pet dies when you die. Dismissing it releases the bond and sends it toward its home; if it cannot get there within two minutes, it remains wild where it is.

entries.title: Travel with companions
entries.summary: Companions follow their owner and help against hostile characters.
body: A companion can help against enemies you damage or enemies that damage you. It will not attack you, your other companions or a dead target.
You and your companion cannot harm each other. Party protection also covers allied companions and summons.
Ask a companion to stop following and it waits while keeping its bond. Dismiss it to end its assistance and return it to ordinary behavior.

entries.title: Elite enemies and bosses
entries.summary: Stronger foes change the rhythm of a fight.
body: Elites and bosses adjust their pursuit when you try to escape. Ordinary elite enemies become 50% faster at half Health; this transition does not itself increase their damage or Health.
Some final bosses have their own encounter phases. New Game+ and New Game++ separately increase character Health and damage throughout the world, including allies and companions.

entries.title: Break an enemy’s guard
entries.summary: Enemies spend Stamina to defend, just as you do.
body: An enemy’s equipment and fighting style influence how often it blocks. Shield users are more likely to guard than other melee fighters and may time their defense for a parry.
Enemies regenerate Stamina after a short pause following expenditure. Pressure their guard, but watch for a shield parry before committing to another melee swing.

entries.title: Face a group
entries.summary: Enemy groups coordinate their attacks and make use of openings.
body: Enemies sharing a target space their spell casts and avoid immediately repeating the same spell. A control spell can set up a stronger attack from another caster.

Normally two melee attackers can press the same target at once, dropping to one while that target is knocked down. Waiting enemies reposition and take turns. Bosses follow their own positioning behavior.

entries.title: Enemy recovery
entries.summary: Some enemies can recover Health and Stamina during a fight.
body: An enemy’s food and hydration condition can supply ongoing Health or Stamina recovery while that resource is below maximum. Starved enemies gain no food recovery, and dehydrated enemies gain no hydration recovery.

entries.title: Food and water
entries.summary: Plan your supplies around two separate fullness limits.
body: Food capacity starts at 100 and water capacity at 50. Four capacity ranks can add 25 each, reaching 200 food or 150 water. You cannot consume an item whose full amount would exceed the remaining capacity.
Food and water diminish with time in the world, including time skipped by waiting. They do not drain while you are offline, and Arena play pauses depletion.
Preservation reduces depletion by 10% per rank, up to 30%. The food states are Well Fed, Fed, Hungry and Starved; water states are Hydrated, Thirsty, Parched and Dehydrated.

entries.title: Recover and endure
entries.summary: Utility perks help you spend less Stamina and get more from supplies.
body: Conditioning improves Stamina regeneration by 25%. Evasive reduces dodge cost by 25%; Guarded reduces block costs by 25%.
Stamina regeneration resumes one second after you spend Stamina. Recovery halves that delay. Its choices offer +25 carry capacity with Pack Rat or +10 Stealth Rating with Light Footed.

Food Recovery and Water Recovery add 25% recovery per rank, up to four ranks. Sustenance adds 15%. Nourished adds 25% food healing; Refreshed adds 25% drink Stamina recovery. These bonuses add together without extending a consumable’s duration.

entries.title: The price of Dark magic
entries.summary: At 100 Dark Points, corruption permanently changes your character.
body: Corruption reduces maximum Health, maximum Stamina and Stamina regeneration by 10%. Lowering Dark Points afterward does not cure it, and the reductions do not stack repeatedly.
In exchange, Dark cooldowns are 25% shorter. Invisibility and Fear last 25% longer, and Void Pulse pushes 25% farther.
Corrupted characters cannot cast Holy magic, though they can still own and equip a Holy Relief. Corruption also lets a rank-4 animal tamer bond with Demon Goats and Minotaurs.

entries.title: Fight together safely
entries.summary: Party protection keeps allies from harming one another.
body: Party members are protected from each other’s attacks, techniques, spells, traps and ongoing damage. Their companions and summons are protected too. Healing and helpful buffs remain available.
Players outside a party can only fight if both enable friendly fire. Vengeance marks do not bypass this agreement.
Arena matches use their own team rules. Certain story encounters can place players on opposing sides for that encounter.

entries.title: Revive a teammate
entries.summary: A living teammate can give a fallen adventurer a second chance.
body: When another eligible human teammate is alive, a fallen player has 60 seconds to be revived. Hold the interaction at their body for five seconds to restore them in place with 15% Health.

After revival, that player cannot be downed again for one real-time hour. Waiting, reloading and travel do not shorten the cooldown. Solo play, Arena combat and some story defeats use immediate death instead.

If an ordinary campaign guest cannot be revived, they leave through the death menu rather than respawning in the session. An unrevived host ends the current campaign attempt for guests, who follow when the host continues. PvP and certain story encounters have separate death rules.

entries.title: Yield or seek vengeance
entries.summary: A death caused by another player offers a choice without failing the campaign.
body: If a player outside your party damaged you within the last 30 seconds, your death counts as PvP even if an enemy landed the final blow. Eligible teammate revival remains available.
If you are not revived, choose Yield to respawn without a penalty, or Seek Vengeance to mark every player involved in that damage window.
A vengeance mark tracks a marked player while they are online and alive. It clears when that player dies by any cause. Both players must still opt into friendly fire to fight.

entries.title: Enter the Arena
entries.summary: Fight team-elimination rounds with temporary high-level builds.
body: Arena fighters use temporary level-100 builds with all skills maximized. In random-loadout matches, each round gives you a new random loadout.

Only opposing teams can damage each other during an active round. Preparation and countdown are protected. There is no respawn during a round; elimination or staying out of bounds too long removes you.
Rounds last up to three minutes. Multiplayer is first to three wins; solo is first to two. A timeout or simultaneous elimination draws the round without awarding a point.
Arena battles do not change campaign XP, Karma, crime, reputation or memories, and food and water do not drain.

entries.title: Choose your Core Traits
entries.summary: Strength, Agility, Stamina, Vitality and Charisma shape your journey.
body: Spend all your Core Trait points before beginning: 12 in New Game, 18 in New Game+ and 25 in New Game++. Each trait can receive up to five points.
Each point in Strength gives +15 Attack Rating. Agility gives +5 Stealth Rating. Stamina and Vitality each add 5% to their maximum resource. Charisma gives +5 starting social standing.
These choices are fixed for the journey. Gaining a level does not automatically add Core Trait points.

entries.title: New Game+ and beyond
entries.summary: A later journey strengthens the characters you meet as well as the enemies you face.
body: New Game+ multiplies character maximum Health and outgoing attack damage by 1.2. New Game++ raises that multiplier to 1.4.
The increase applies throughout the world, including neutral characters, allies and companions. Becoming your companion does not remove that increase.

entries.title: Levels and Core Traits
entries.summary: Experience and your starting traits serve different roles.
body: Your level grows with experience. Your Core Trait allocation is chosen for the journey and does not automatically rise when you level up.
Use the Skills menu to spend earned skill points on perk ranks, and check equipment and active effects for changes to your Health, Stamina and combat strength.

entries.title: Set a trap
entries.summary: Catch pursuers in a bear trap or hang them from a rope snare.
body: Use a trap item to place it. A green or red preview shows whether the position is valid; rope snares require a suitable tree point. A trap arms after two seconds.
A bear trap deals one damage hit and roots its victim. A rope snare hoists its victim beneath the branch. Mash Interact if you are caught; enemies struggle to escape on their own.
Your traps do not catch you or your allies. Improved Rope Snare ranks require more escape presses.

entries.title: Draw and release a bow
entries.summary: Each arrow needs a complete draw before it can fly.
body: Hold attack to draw, then release to shoot. A quick tap that ends before the bow is ready does not fire an arrow. After a shot, the bow recovers for 0.35 seconds.
Keep attack held through recovery to begin the next draw. Canceling or holstering an unfinished shot returns its arrow to your quiver; the next arrow is readied automatically.

entries.title: Dodge
entries.summary: Move and roll to escape a strike or cancel a melee swing.
body: While moving, press Q on keyboard or click the controller’s right stick to dodge in your movement direction. Pressing dodge while standing still does nothing.
A dodge costs 15 Stamina. Evasive reduces this to 11.25. You cannot dodge while mounted, climbing, swimming, trapped or unable to move.

entries.title: Heavy attacks
entries.summary: Hold attack to commit to a stronger blow.
body: Tap attack for a light swing, or hold it beyond 0.2 seconds for a heavy attack that deals 1.5 times the damage.
An unblocked heavy hit interrupts and briefly staggers ordinary enemies. Elites are staggered less, while bosses resist this heavy-hit stagger.

entries.title: Lock on
entries.summary: Keep a dangerous enemy in view while you fight.
body: Press F, or hold RB and click the right stick, to lock onto the eligible enemy nearest the center of your view. Press again to release the lock.
The camera follows the target, and its name, level and Health appear at the top of the screen. A dead or vanished target releases the lock or allows another enemy to be selected.

entries.title: Pocket Sand
entries.summary: Blind nearby enemies to create a brief opening.
body: Equip Pocket Sand as your throwable, then use Throw. It affects hostile enemies in a short cone ahead of your hand, with walls blocking the burst.

Each throw consumes one Pocket Sand and starts a 12-second cooldown, even if you miss. Blindness refreshes rather than adding durations. Blinded enemies lose sight and pause their behavior; a blinded player sees a sand overlay.

entries.title: Switch your target
entries.summary: Use a deliberate flick to change enemies while locked on.
body: Ordinary camera movement keeps your current target. A strong right-stick flick or fast mouse swipe switches to another enemy.
If your target dies or disappears, the lock can select another target or release.

entries.title: Shadow Step
entries.summary: Replace your dodge with a teleport behind a locked-on enemy.
body: After learning Shadow Step, equip it in the Dodge row of the Techniques page. Your dodge button then steps behind a locked-on enemy within ten metres and turns you to face it.
Gain 30% movement speed for three seconds. If the target is invalid, the ability is on cooldown or no safe space exists behind it, you perform an ordinary dodge and pay only that dodge’s cost.
Rank 2 gives 50 extra percentage points of rear damage on your next qualifying hit against that target within five seconds. With Blindside rank 3, the combined bonus is 75%.

stats.label: Cooldown
stats.value: 20 s (persists through unequip / weapon change / respawn)

entries.title: Keep Arena fights separate
entries.summary: Arena matches use temporary characters and leave your campaign progress intact.
body: Arena items, deaths, experience and reputation changes do not carry back into the campaign. Arena rounds use their own teams and combat rules.
You do not create a campaign character or earn campaign XP and Karma in the Arena.

entries.title: Share the fight, earn the experience
entries.summary: Every contributor receives the full kill XP.
body: Damage an enemy yourself, or through your companion, and you receive the full experience award when it dies. The award is not divided between players, and the final blow is not required.
Players who do not contribute damage receive no kill XP. Training Arena kills award half the normal XP. PvP Arena kills award none.
Kill Karma can go to each contributor. Training and Jester-performance kills do not award Karma.

entries.title: Share your loot
entries.summary: Corpses and chests hold one shared inventory.
body: When one player takes an item, it is gone for everyone else. There are no separate loot copies for each party member.
Training and Jester-performance enemies drop no loot. Taking an item owned by a character or faction counts as theft by the player who takes it.

entries.title: Share a Relief
entries.summary: Your deployed Relief can help another caster, but remains yours to recall.
body: A player holding a Relief of the matching school can cast through your deployed board while inside its influence. Only one caster uses a board at a time.
Only the deployer can recall the board. A spell already being written finishes before a normal recall closes it.
Enemy-owned Reliefs are private to their casters and cannot be looted or borrowed.

entries.title: Read the wildlife
entries.summary: Animals can hear your approach and defend themselves.
body: Bears, deer, moose, goats and other animals have their own attacks. Prey animals can hear an approach farther away than people, and sprinting is louder than walking.
Animals do not act as social witnesses, and attacking an animal is not recorded as assault or a crime. A monster such as a Wendigo is not treated as an ordinary animal.

entries.title: Fight creatures
entries.summary: Watch a creature’s own movements to read its attacks.
body: Creatures such as bears, moose, goats and Wendigos attack with their own strikes and reaches. Face a blockable strike to guard against it, and learn the timing of each creature rather than relying on one universal attack rhythm.

entries.title: Close on an archer
entries.summary: Archers fight at range, but losing a bow forces a change of plan.
body: Bow-wielding enemies draw and shoot from a distance and may use Arrowstorm. If they lose their usable bow, they switch to melee; an archer without a sidearm fights with fists.

entries.title: Fight enemy casters
entries.summary: Enemy casters mix weapon attacks with their own Relief magic.
body: A caster can deploy a Relief, write and release spells, then return to weapons or fists. While the board is deployed, the caster can attack at range with its school’s bolt.
Some casters heal themselves or protect allies. An enemy’s board closes when its owner dies and cannot be looted.

entries.title: Watch for thief traps
entries.summary: A thief may leave a trap in your path as you close in.
body: Thieves can place bear traps during a fight. If you step in one, it damages and holds you until you break free by repeatedly pressing Interact.
They carry limited traps, cannot trigger their own, and need a suitable tree point to place a rope snare.

entries.title: Wendigos
entries.summary: Treat a Wendigo as a boss-level threat.
body: Wendigos fight with close-range clawing attacks. Watch their movement, keep space to dodge and look for an opening after a committed strike.

entries.title: Crouch and sneak
entries.summary: Lower your profile to move more quietly and stay out of sight.
body: Crouching makes you harder to see and hear, lets darkness conceal you at closer range and enables pickpocketing. A detection eye replaces the crosshair to show how visible you are.

Crouching adds +5 Stealth Rating, reduces sight detection to 55% of its standing rate and caps ordinary footstep reach at ten metres. Different parts of stealth use these bonuses differently, so the extra rating is not a universal bonus to every stealth check.

entries.title: Invisibility and witnesses
entries.summary: Dark Invisibility can hide your identity from witnesses.
body: While invisible, witnesses cannot identify you as the person committing an assault. This concealment does not erase what a witness already knows about you.

entries.title: Hide in deep darkness
entries.summary: Dark places can break sight, but they do not silence your movement.
body: In deep darkness, ordinary enemies cannot visually find you from more than ten metres away, or five metres while you crouch.

If an enemy has already recognized you, darkness breaks its current sight after a short delay. It remembers who you were and searches your last known position. Walls break sight immediately; footsteps can still give you away.
Darkness is not a guarantee against witnesses to a violent act or Dark casting. Escape and concealment do not erase an incident already remembered.

entries.title: Keep your footsteps quiet
entries.summary: Sprinting and landing carry farther than ordinary steps.
body: Ordinary footsteps are limited to 15 metres while standing and ten metres while crouched, with actual hearing depending on the listener. Sprinting doubles the reach; landing from a jump increases it by half.
Stealth Rating and Feather Quiet reduce footstep noise. Crouching lowers the range cap and adds its Stealth bonus, but does not make you silent.

entries.title: From suspicion to combat
entries.summary: A glimpse or a sound is different from being recognized.
body: An enemy does not begin a fight just because it half-noticed you or heard a sound. Recognition while you are visible, or direct contact such as your attack, can trigger combat and alert nearby allies.
Break sight behind cover or in deep darkness to make an enemy search instead of continuously tracking you.

entries.title: Read the detection eye
entries.summary: Light, distance and movement affect how quickly you are noticed.
body: You are harder to identify at a distance, in shadow, while crouched or still, and near the edge of someone’s view. Standing close in bright light or sprinting straight ahead makes recognition much faster.
Break line of sight to let an uncertain glimpse fade. Cover that hides both your head and body blocks sight.
The detection eye helps you read the change from being glimpsed to being recognized.

entries.title: Throw a distraction
entries.summary: Send a guard toward a sound instead of your hiding place.
body: Use a Throwing Stone from your inventory or quick-use slot. It makes a noise where it first lands, drawing listeners to that spot.
Each throw consumes one stone. Carry up to 20 in a stack.

entries.title: After respawning
entries.summary: Respawning restores Health and Stamina without clearing corruption.
body: You return with full maximum Health, including your Vitality bonus, and full Stamina. Food and water fullness stay where they were, but any meal or drink recovery still running stops.
Corruption remains after death. Check the separate co-op revival rules, since a downed teammate and a respawning character return in different ways.

entries.title: Build your skills
entries.summary: Spend skill points on the abilities that suit your approach.
body: Open Player Info, then Skills. The seven branches are Melee, Reliefs, Sneak, Speech, Utility, Weapon Techniques and Dirty Tricks.
Each perk rank costs one skill point. Linked prerequisites must be met and each perk has a maximum rank. Purchases are permanent, so review a perk before committing your points.

entries.title: Quick and Deadly, Feather Quiet
entries.summary: Improve your stealth rating or focus on quieter movement.
body: Quick and Deadly sets its Stealth Rating contribution to 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50 across five ranks. It helps stealth-related actions such as critical hits and pickpocketing.
Feather Quiet reduces footstep loudness by 5%, 10%, 20%, 30% or 75%. It does not make you less visible. Crouching adds its separate +5 Stealth Rating bonus.

entries.title: Begin a Relief spell
entries.summary: Hold the matching Relief and stand within a free board’s influence.
body: To cast a school’s spells, wield its Relief and stand inside a deployed Relief of the same school. It can be yours or another player’s. Only one caster can use a board at a time.
If the nearest board is busy, another available board in range can serve you. If no suitable board is free, the cast is refused and costs nothing.
Short messages explain blocked casts, including locked spells, cooldowns, inactive Reliefs, full Health or insufficient resources. A Blood sacrifice requires more Health than its cost.

entries.title: Deploy your Relief
entries.summary: Place a board to create a space for casting its school’s spells.
body: With a Relief wielded, use the deploy action to throw it in front of you. The board settles and grows, spreading its influence around it.
Stand inside that influence while holding the matching school’s Relief to begin casting. You can deploy one board per school, so several schools can be active at once.
Corrupted characters cannot deploy a Holy Relief.

entries.title: Interrupted spells
entries.summary: A cast broken before release keeps its resources and cooldown.
body: If a heavy hit, freeze, weapon switch or another interruption breaks your spell before release, its letters fade and you keep the Stamina, Health and Dark Points that would have been charged. Its cooldown does not begin.
Once the spell visibly releases, its cost and cooldown are committed. Interrupting you afterward does not cancel or refund that spell.
A normal recall waits for an already-started cast to finish. Simply stepping outside the influence after beginning a cast does not by itself cancel it.

entries.title: Recall your Relief
entries.summary: Bring your board back after its active casting is finished.
body: Use recall after the deployed board finishes growing and its three-second recall lock has passed. Only its deployer can recall it.
Recall stops new casts immediately. Anyone already writing a spell finishes on the full-size board before it shrinks back to your hand.
With several schools deployed, recall returns the board matching the Relief you are holding.

entries.title: Read the spell in the air
entries.summary: Each school writes its magic with a different supernatural script.
body: As a spell is written on the board, its letters take shape overhead. Blood forms dripping blackletter, Holy draws golden letters in light, and Dark pulls a restless script from shadow.
The completed word releases with the spell. If the cast is interrupted, the letters dissolve.

entries.title: Wield a Relief
entries.summary: A Relief is both a carried weapon and the focus of a magic school.
body: Wield a Holy, Blood or Dark Relief to use that school’s unlocked spells, deploy and recall its board, or defend with a held-board swing and block.
While the board is deployed, it leaves your hand and enables the school’s ranged bolt. Putting the Relief away removes access to its wielded abilities until you equip it again.
Enemy-owned boards cannot be kept or looted.

entries.title: Cast together
entries.summary: Share boards while keeping your own spells and progression.
body: Players can cast through another player’s available Relief of the matching school. Each board serves one caster at a time; a busy board can be bypassed by using another free one in range.
Each player keeps their own unlocks, mastery, Dark Points, corruption and selected Ultimates.
When allied players use Fear on the same enemy, their durations add together. Freeze does not add durations in the same way.

entries.title: Equip a Relief quickly
entries.summary: Choose a board from the weapon wheel and release to equip it.
body: Hold T on keyboard or LB on controller to open the weapon wheel. Highlight a Relief, then release the button to equip it in your main hand.
If you made a different click selection in the wheel, that selection takes priority. Other weapons keep their usual click-to-equip behavior.

entries.title: Master a school of magic
entries.summary: Unlock a spell, enhance it, then master its additional effect.
body: Each school has five ranks each in Unlock, Level Up and Mastery. Rank 1 applies to spell slot 1, and so on. A spell must be unlocked before enhancement and enhanced before mastery.
Rank 5 applies to whichever Ultimate you have selected for that school. Swapping Ultimates keeps the same slot mastery.

Mastery adds new benefits while retaining enhanced strength: Holy can share healing and protection, Blood gains stronger sustain and a lasting summon, and Dark gains effects such as a spreading Curse and longer Void Stasis. Read each spell for its exact benefit.

entries.title: Train with the Cursed Doll
entries.summary: Face a region’s enemies one at a time without changing the world outside.
body: Ask a regional Doll to take you to the Training Arena, then begin a run beside the Arena Doll. Enemies from that region arrive one at a time in a shuffled order.
Kills award half the usual XP and no loot. Training does not create crimes or change the world. Dying or falling out ends the run and returns you beside the Arena Doll.
Leave to return to the regional Doll you came from.

entries.title: Templar armor: recover near magic
entries.summary: Templar pieces restore Health while you stand within a Relief’s influence.
body: Each equipped Templar piece restores 1% of maximum Health per second inside a Holy, Blood or Dark Relief’s influence. A full five-piece set restores 5% per second.
Leaving the influence ends this regeneration. Enemies wearing Templar armor receive the same benefit.

entries.title: Travel with the Cursed Doll
entries.summary: Discover a waypoint, then return to it through the Doll’s travel map.
body: Walk into a travel waypoint to discover it and earn 100 XP once. Speak to a regional Cursed Doll to open her travel map or visit the Training Arena.
The map offers discovered waypoints with available arrival points. Choose one to travel beside that Doll. You do not need to complete training to unlock a discovered destination.

entries.title: Ride through the realm
entries.summary: Mount a horse to cover ground with a different pace and perspective.
body: Look at a horse and press Interact to mount. Steer forward, pull back to reverse slowly, or turn in place while stopped. Turning while moving makes a wider curve.
Hold Left Shift, or use L3 on controller, to sprint. Interact while moving quickly brakes the horse before you dismount.
Weapons are put away when you mount and cannot be drawn while riding.

entries.title: Explore your map
entries.summary: Reveal the world as you travel, one discovery at a time.
body: Unexplored ground is black on the minimap and world map. Moving through the realm reveals the area within 60 metres and keeps that exploration for your character.
Every player has their own explored map, including players sharing a screen. Training Arenas and Jester performances do not reveal campaign ground.

entries.title: Open locked doors and chests
entries.summary: Use the right key, or risk a noisy lock-picking attempt.
body: A locked door or chest offers Unlock when you carry its key. Otherwise, choose Pick Lock to attempt a short timing challenge.
Respond with Interact to three to five prompts, depending on difficulty. A missed prompt makes noise, and being seen tampering can count as a crime under local law.
Walk away to abandon the attempt.

entries.title: Pick a pocket
entries.summary: Get close without being noticed, then choose what to take.
body: Crouch behind a character, or approach beside one who is asleep, and choose Pickpocket within reach. Higher Stealth improves your chance of taking an item.
